summary: Opaque native.node binary loaded via require() with credential-store and process/network capability surface
details: Package ships a single ~10MB Linux x86_64 ELF Node native addon (tools.linux-x64-gnu.node) as its `main`, so a consumer's `require()` dlopens the binary and executes its NAPI init function on the installer's process. The tarball contains no JavaScript wrapper, no source, and a one-line README that does not describe any function. The manifest omits `repository`, `homepage`, `author`, `bugs`, and `description`; the version string embeds a Unix timestamp and a build-farm suffix, and the package name does not correspond to any documented project. Strings inside the binary reveal a capability set that includes an HTTP/TLS client (ureq), SQLite with authentication (SQLITE_AUTH_USER), subprocess/PTY spawning (posix_spawnp), privilege primitives (setuid), dynamic loading (dlopen), and host fingerprinting (getifaddrs, /dev/disk/by-id/, /etc/lsb-release), together with credential-store-shaped strings such as "Found login for" — a combination consistent with a browser/credential stealer with network exfiltration, not with any advertised functionality. Because the payload is a compiled opaque binary invoked on module load, the specific exfiltration endpoints cannot be extracted from source, but the shape of the loaded code and the absence of any legitimate declared purpose indicate an installer-side active-attack surface delivered as a platform-specific native meta-package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
